name: Clean a messy lead CSV export into importable rows

parameters.content:
### How it works
Lead exports rarely import cleanly: the header says `E-MAIL` or `Last-Name ` (stray space),
values carry leading spaces, one address is `ANA.KOVAC@PrimaStudio.rs`, the next is
`marko.petrovic@ petroco.rs`. This workflow fixes that before the data reaches a CRM or a
cold-email tool.
Press **Execute workflow**. It reads the CSV in **Messy lead CSV (paste yours)**, maps the
header row onto `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `company`, `domain`, `phone` (header text
may be anything), splits fields with quotes and commas correctly, trims every value,
lowercases and space-strips the address, validates it, derives the domain when the column is
empty, and adds `full_name`. Rows that cannot be fixed come back in `rejected` with a
`reason` instead of disappearing. **Summarize the report** returns `rows_in`, `valid_rows`,
`rejected_rows`, `cleaned_leads` and `rejected`.

### Setup
Nothing to connect: no credentials, no HTTP requests, no file paths, no data leaving your
n8n instance. Open **Messy lead CSV (paste yours)** and replace the sample rows with your own
export, keeping the header row. To read a file instead, put *Read/Write Files from Disk* and
*Extract from File* (CSV) in front of **Clean and validate rows**.

### Customization
Add a synonym to the header matcher if your export names a column differently. The email rule
is pragmatic, not RFC 5322: loosen it for unusual addresses. Remove the `phone` mapping if you
do not want phone numbers in the output.

Limitations: quoted fields containing commas and semicolons are handled; fields with embedded
line breaks are not. Nothing here checks whether a mailbox exists or a domain has MX records -
formatting is cleaned, deliverability is not.

Free template from the LeadFlow project - two more free workflows (dedupe, email patterns) and a browser version: https://fejzadenis.github.io/leadflow/free/

parameters.content:
## 1. Paste your export
Header row required. Columns are matched by name, so the order does not matter.

## 2. Clean, validate, report
Trim + lowercase, validate, derive the domain, list what could not be fixed.
